title: Past, perfect and clause order — in sentences
summary: Use the English meaning as well as the Swedish context to choose or type the missing word or phrase. Use har + supine for the perfect. A finished time such as i går normally takes the preterite. In a subordinate clause, inte comes before the finite verb.

s01.sentenceGloss: She has already read the book.

s02.sentenceGloss: I have read the book twice.

s03.sentenceGloss: Yesterday I read the whole book.
s03.note: The finished time i går takes the preterite läste.

s04.sentenceGloss: We have walked home from the station.

s05.note: The supine of äta is ätit.

s06.note: The supine of komma is kommit.

s07.sentenceGloss: I read a book when I am not working.
s07.note: När introduces a time clause; inte comes before arbetar.

s08.sentenceGloss: Today she has not read the newspaper.
s08.note: Main clause: I dag + har + subject + inte.
